findings.finding: The reviewer's findings table could not be read, so its rows are not listed here: aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/infrastructure-design/infrastructure-specification.md: findings table header declares #, Severity, Location, Finding, Recommendation. Expected columns: ID, Severity, Location, Finding, Required action, Status. Missing: ID, Required action, Status
findings.required_action: Address the reviewer's findings as written below this table.

findings.location: aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/infrastructure-design/infrastructure-specification.md > Infrastructure Services > API Gateway HTTP API row, and the illustrative CDK snippet (`addRoutes` for `/v1/{proxy+}` and `/health`)
findings.finding: The contract (contract-summary.md OpenAPI) sets `servers: - url: /v1` and lists `/health` under `paths` with `security: []`, so the contract's open health URL is `/v1/health`. The design routes an open `/health` at the root and puts the JWT authorizer on `/v1/{proxy+}`. A caller following the contract and calling `GET /v1/health` with no token falls into the `/v1/{proxy+}` route and gets 401, which breaks the contract's "open route, no token required". The root `/health` the design opens is not in the contract. The smoke test (cicd-pipeline.md stage 13) checks the root path, so it would not catch this.
findings.required_action: Add a specific `GET /v1/health` route with no authorizer (HTTP API picks the most specific route, so it wins over `/v1/{proxy+}`) and point the smoke test at it. Keep or drop the root `/health` as an explicit choice. Alternatively, get the contract changed so the health check sits outside `/v1`. Either way, the route table and the contract must give the same URL.

findings.location: aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/infrastructure-design/monitoring-design.md > Alerts > Elevated 5xx, and SLIs / SLOs > Availability
findings.finding: The only alarm that can page, and the 99.9% availability SLI, are both worked out from the service's own log line (`statusCode`, `outcome=InternalError`). That line is written only when a request finishes inside the Lambda. Failures that hit callers hardest never produce it: a Lambda timeout (10 s), a crash or out-of-memory, a throttle at the ~50 reserved-concurrency cap, or a gateway integration error. The infrastructure specification itself says these come back as the gateway's own 5xx body. So the alarm misses them, they are left out of the SLI's denominator, and measured availability looks better than it is.
findings.required_action: Base the 5xx alarm and the availability SLI on the edge: the HTTP API `5xx` and `Count` CloudWatch metrics, or a metric filter on the access-log `status` field. Keep the app-log `InternalError` filter as a second signal for diagnosis. Say whether 401s count toward total requests in the SLI.

findings.location: aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/infrastructure-design/infrastructure-specification.md > Infrastructure Services > DynamoDB table `Item` (failed-condition handling); traceability.json NFR1.2
findings.finding: Upstream performance-design.md (Bounded retry row) says to retry internally on a conditional-check failure, treating it as transient contention. This design says that on a failed condition the repository reads the item once to tell ItemNotFound from InsufficientStock from overflow. The two contradict each other, and nothing here says which errors the ≤3 retry in NFR1.2 actually covers. With `SET quantity = quantity + :delta`, a failed condition is never contention: DynamoDB applies single-item updates one at a time. The follow-up read also races: if a concurrent increment lands between the failed update and the read, the read shows a state that would pass, and the design does not say what happens next. On the path the team calls its most important, a developer has to guess.
findings.required_action: State that on ConditionalCheckFailedException the repository classifies and does not retry. Use `ReturnValuesOnConditionCheckFailure: ALL_OLD` on the UpdateItem so the item as it was at the failed check comes back with the error, with no second read and no race. Say what the bounded retry covers: throttling or internal-server errors only, beyond the AWS SDK's own default retries. Update the NFR1.2 target to match.

findings.location: aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/infrastructure-design/infrastructure-specification.md > DynamoDB table `Item` Notes ("No secondary indexes at MVP; every access is by sku") and IAM execution role row; traceability.json NFR1.4, NFR1.9
findings.finding: WF3 in functional-spec.md lists all items with `limit`, `offset` up to 10000, and a `total` count. On a table whose only key is `sku`, with no secondary index, a DynamoDB Query needs an equality condition on one `sku`, so it cannot list across items. The design's "DynamoDB Query with Limit (≤100) serving bounded pagination" cannot be built as written. DynamoDB also has no offset: serving offset 10000 means reading and discarding 10000+ items, and `total` means counting the whole table. That makes the OK claims for NFR1.9 ("per-request work bounded independent of total item count") and NFR1.4 false, and contradicts performance-design.md's "no unbounded scans". The IAM row also lists Query as the list permission and leaves out Scan.
findings.required_action: Pick and document the list access pattern. One option is a Scan with Limit plus a stated item-count ceiling for the MVP. Another is a GSI on a constant partition key with `sku` as sort key, or a maintained counter item for `total`. Say how `offset` and `total` are served and what they cost. Mark NFR1.9 as a known limit (or N/A with a ceiling) instead of OK if work grows with offset and table size. Fix the IAM action list to match.

findings.location: aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/infrastructure-design/monitoring-design.md > Alerts > Health failing; traceability.json NFR1.13, NFR3.1
findings.finding: Nothing calls `/health` on a schedule: the design names no CloudWatch Synthetics canary or Route 53 health check, so the "`/health` returning non-200" condition has nothing to measure it. The NFR1.13 target "API Gateway routes only to healthy integration" is also wrong about AWS: API Gateway does not health-check a Lambda integration or route around one. Readiness and liveness probes (NFR3.1 target) do not exist for Lambda either.
findings.required_action: Name the probe, for example a Synthetics canary on the open health URL every 5 minutes with an alarm on its success metric, or drop that part of the alert condition. Reword NFR1.13 and NFR3.1 to describe what Lambda and the probe actually do.

findings.location: aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/infrastructure-design/infrastructure-specification.md > AWS Lambda `InventoryApi` row ("auto-scaling via concurrency target tracking")
findings.finding: On-demand Lambda concurrency has no target-tracking scaling. Target tracking through Application Auto Scaling applies only to provisioned concurrency, which this design does not use. The real controls here are on-demand scaling plus the reserved-concurrency cap.
findings.required_action: Drop "concurrency target tracking". State on-demand scaling capped by reserved concurrency of 50.

findings.location: aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/infrastructure-design/cicd-pipeline.md > Deployment strategy and Rollback; infrastructure-specification.md CDK snippet (`LambdaProxy(fn)`)
findings.finding: Rollback relies on moving a Lambda alias back to the previous version, but the snippet points the HTTP API integration at the function itself (`fn`), not at an alias. If the gateway calls `$LATEST`, moving the alias changes nothing.
findings.required_action: Say that each deploy publishes a version, that a `live` alias points at it, and that the HTTP API integration targets that alias.

findings.location: aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/infrastructure-design/infrastructure-specification.md > DynamoDB table `Item` Configuration, versus cicd-pipeline.md > Rollback > Data and identity safety
findings.finding: cicd-pipeline.md says the table has deletion protection. The table's configuration in the infrastructure specification (and its snippet) lists PITR and encryption but no deletion protection and no retain-on-delete removal policy.
findings.required_action: Add `deletionProtection: true` and a RETAIN removal policy to the table configuration so the two documents agree.

findings.location: aidlc/spaces/default/intents/260825-inventory-api/construction/inventory-api/infrastructure-design/cicd-pipeline.md > stage 13 Smoke test; infrastructure-specification.md > Cognito user pool row
findings.finding: A user created with `admin-create-user` starts in FORCE_CHANGE_PASSWORD status. `initiate-auth` with USER_PASSWORD_AUTH then returns a NEW_PASSWORD_REQUIRED challenge, not tokens. Nothing says who creates the smoke-test user or makes its password permanent, so the first merge-blocking smoke run would fail.
findings.required_action: Say how the smoke-test user is provisioned (CDK custom resource or a one-time runbook step) and that its password is set with `admin-set-user-password --permanent` from the Secrets Manager value.

findings.finding: cdk-nag reports Errors and Warnings, not High. In the AwsSolutions pack, a Cognito user pool without MFA (AwsSolutions-COG2) or without advanced security set to enforced (AwsSolutions-COG3) is an Error, so the new auth stack would fail stage 10 as designed unless a suppression is planned.
findings.required_action: Define the gate as "no unsuppressed cdk-nag Errors". Either list the planned, justified suppressions (for example COG2 and COG3 for an admin-created MVP user pool) or turn on the matching Cognito settings.

findings.finding: The NFR design defines 32 ids (NFR1.1 to 1.16, NFR2.1 to 2.5, NFR3.1 to 3.9, NFR4.1 to 4.2). `upstream_ids` lists 28. NFR3.3, NFR3.4, NFR3.8 and NFR3.9, all defined in observability-design.md, are only in `reverse`. Other N/A and Deferred ids (NFR1.3, NFR1.5, NFR3.2) sit in `coverage`, so the file treats the same kind of id two ways.
findings.required_action: List all 32 NFR-design ids in `upstream_ids`. Move the four into `coverage` with their existing N/A or Deferred status and reasons.

### Summary

The auth revision mostly holds up. The Cognito pool, the no-secret client, the JWT authorizer with the gateway's 401 body, 401s captured in the access logs, and the corrected condition bounds all match the contract and the functional design. Four Major gaps block READY: the contract's open health URL `/v1/health` would get 401 behind `/v1/{proxy+}`; the paging 5xx alarm and the availability SLI miss gateway-side failures such as timeouts and throttles; the adjustment path's retry and classification contradict the upstream design and race; and listing items with a Query and offset and total cannot be built on a table keyed only by `sku`.
